paper_metadata.title: Effect of surface recrystallization on high-temperature tensile properties of a directionally solidified DZ409 Ni-based superalloy

evidence.quote: This study systematically investigated the effect of RX on the high-temperature tensile properties of a DS DZ409 superalloy.

evidence.section: 4.1 Morpholgies of surface RX layers before tensile test
evidence.quote: After 15 s of sandblasting, a thin, discontinuous RX layer composed of fine grains forms, with an average thickness of approximately 17 µm, where the GBs are chaotically arranged.

evidence.section: 4.1 Morpholgies of surface RX layers before tensile test
evidence.quote: After 45 s, the layer becomes nearly continuous, and the grains grow significantly larger, with an average thickness of about 56 µm, and the GBs are predominantly vertical to the matrix.

evidence.section: 4.1 Morpholgies of surface RX layers before tensile test
evidence.quote: Additionally, a small number of micropores are observed in the DS matrix, and these micropores can accelerate the propagation rate of cracks that originate from the RX layer within the matrix and reduce the mechanical properties of the DS superalloy.

evidence.section: 4.2 Influence of surface RX on high-temperature tensile properties at 650 °C and 950 °C
evidence.quote: As the RX fraction increases, the yield strength decreases almost linearly from approximately 1,171 MPa to about 988 MPa.

Due to the lower strength of the RX layer and the inhomogeneous deformation between this layer and the DS matrix, cracks can readily initiate at the GBs in the early stages of tensile testing.
Subsequently, these cracks propagate along the grain boundaries into the DS matrix, as illustrated in Fig. 8, leading to the failure of the DS specimens.
